correspondence.component_scope: Chosen unnamed Palmetto Mountains opening and Palmetto Wash junction
correspondence.finding: The opening occupies the southwest-descending incised feeder on the western Palmetto Mountains flank. The original relief depicts its enclosing canyon and the direct meeting with the east-west Palmetto Wash corridor alongside the highway. The generalized initial bend remains within that feeder and its receiving junction; no neighboring named headwater or spring is substituted.
correspondence.name_scope: The selected opening is unnamed in the inspected cartography. Palmetto Wash is the receiving named wash.

correspondence.component_scope: Palmetto Wash through the southern mountain passage
correspondence.finding: Repeated Palmetto Wash labels follow the selected westward and northwestward bends beside the highway through the same canyon, including the turn around the southern spur and the opening onto the southeastern Fish Lake Valley floor. Both original scales depict the same canyon-to-fan passage.
correspondence.name_scope: Palmetto Wash is supported only for the directly named wash corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Palmetto Wash fan and northward turn onto the valley floor
correspondence.finding: After leaving the canyon, the selected route turns northwest across the adjoining alluvial receiving floor. The overview shows the intermittent wash continuation and the surrounding lowland together; the southern detail covers its fan, road crossings and transition into the long northward valley axis. The detail omits some minor blue linework that is present in the overview, but there is no separate basin crossing at this mapped fan-to-floor transition.
correspondence.name_scope: No extension of Palmetto Wash over the whole valley floor is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Fish Lake Valley axial floor toward Dyer
correspondence.finding: The selection continues north through the same broad valley bottom between the eastern fans and the western mountain front, passing the agricultural and road setting east of the main north-south highway. The overlapping originals cover the entire interval and its intermittent channel and wet-ground patches. The report independently describes the valley axial drainage as northward toward the northern playa. An individually wetted stream thread through every dry or cultivated patch is neither required nor asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: The southern axial interval is not given a whole-system river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Dyer-area wetland bend and bounded McAfee Creek reach
correspondence.finding: The selected route approaches the wetland east of Dyer, bends west within the low valley floor, and then turns north along the directly labeled McAfee Creek receiving reach. Perry Aiken Creek joins from the west, while the selected southern approach remains distinct from the McAfee mountain headwaters. The originals cover the wet-ground bend, named reach and receiving junction in one continuous valley setting.
correspondence.name_scope: McAfee Creek is a supported bounded reach label. Its unselected western headwaters and Perry Aiken Creek are not substituted for the chosen opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern axial marsh and Chiatovich/Rock Creek receiving wetland
correspondence.finding: North of the McAfee reach, the selected continuation follows the elongated valley-margin wetland and axial drainage past the western tributary entries. It reaches the pond-and-marsh setting receiving Chiatovich Creek and Rock Creek, then continues along its northern margin. The overview and detailed original jointly depict these tributary joins, the wetland passage and the onward axial lowland.
correspondence.name_scope: Chiatovich Creek, Rock Creek and Leidy Creek are adjoining tributary context; no one of these names is applied to the selected whole. No new independent lake name is assigned to the pond-and-marsh setting.

correspondence.component_scope: Fish Lake Valley Marsh approach and playa passage
correspondence.finding: The route crosses the adjoining marshy floor by The Crossing, enters the elongated northern playa directly labeled Fish Lake Valley Marsh, and continues through its interior to the northwestern end. The selected approach, playa floor and outgoing northern tongue are continuously covered by the originals. The report describes runoff ponding and evaporating in this playa, with exceptional northward overflow.
correspondence.name_scope: Fish Lake Valley Marsh is a separate receiving wetland/playa identity, not a whole-feature river hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern playa tongue and The Gap
correspondence.finding: The northern playa tongue leads into the narrow low passage between the Volcanic Hills and the eastern uplands. The original overview depicts the connected drainage and marsh corridor, while the detailed original depicts the same valley passage and Gap Spring surroundings. Rush and Katzer identify this as The Gap and explicitly describe occasional surface outflow from Fish Lake Valley into Columbus Salt Marsh Valley. Their photograph also notes the absence of a persistent carrying channel. These are compatible geographic spillway observations; current overflow and a continuously drawn river through the gap are not completion requirements.
correspondence.name_scope: The Gap is a geographic passage. The source distinguishes the normally ponding Fish Lake Valley drainage from the Columbus receiving basin, so no single natural-river identity is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: The Gap outlet fan and highway crossing into Columbus Salt Marsh
correspondence.finding: Beyond the narrow passage, the selected route occupies the same northward-opening alluvial receiving floor and crosses the east-west highway setting before entering the southern edge of Columbus Salt Marsh. Both map scales show this gap-to-fan-to-playa relationship. The report explicitly identifies Columbus Salt Marsh as the receiving valley for the occasional surface outflow.
correspondence.name_scope: Columbus Salt Marsh is the supported receiving geographic identity, not a river-name extension.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected endpoint inside Columbus Salt Marsh
correspondence.finding: The final northward continuation remains within the large mapped Columbus Salt Marsh playa and ends in its interior wet-ground setting. The actual endpoint is covered, beyond the southern playa edge and highway approach. There is no requirement for a separately drawn river line across this same continuous playa floor.
correspondence.name_scope: The terminal is Columbus Salt Marsh. No additional lake or whole-system river name is invented.

correspondence.component_scope: selected opening and southern transfer; Initial parts1–7, including the southern westward passage
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in the forested Sierra de Santa Cruz hills south of Semococh, approaching the Sechalcate/Chacalté-side headwater drainage and continuing west through Secar–Secoyoute. Cartography depicts separate headwater branches and the Semanzana valley; imagery shows the intervening wooded hill-and-valley terrain. These originals do not establish the entire selected transfer from that eastern opening into the Semanzana-side corridor. The gap concerns drainage through the intervening terrain, rather than precise banks, a missing bend or current flow.

correspondence.component_scope: semanzana western joining corridor; Western headward end and parts8–17; no exact hydronym-boundary vertex
correspondence.finding: The sources distinguish Río Semanzana in the western Livingston hills and its approach to the Chahal river corridor. The USAC account states that Semanzana originates in Livingston and enters Chahal to join Río Chahal. The two municipal maps and upper imagery cover the western approach, road crossings, joining setting and northward low-valley continuation. This relationship does not prove the earlier Sechalcate–Secar transfer or label every initial modeled part Semanzana.

correspondence.component_scope: gracias a dios valley and northern turn; Parts18–27 and join with10580
correspondence.finding: The selected river follows the northward valley and turns east toward Modesto Méndez. Cartography and middle imagery cover the tributary-junction, cultivated valley, wooded hill margins and northern bends continuously. The USAC study describes Chahal and Chiyú forming Gracias a Dios, while CONAP places Gracias a Dios upstream of Sarstún. Chiyú is an unselected joining approach, not a whole-system alias.

correspondence.component_scope: modesto mendez and middle sarstun; All9 parts and both fragment joins
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation passes the Modesto Méndez and Río Franco joining setting into the broad eastward Sarstún corridor. Livingston cartography and middle/lower imagery depict the connected lowland river, bends and adjoining wetlands. Long straight selected portions are ordinary generalized representation of this continuously covered corridor, without imposing the downstream name on all upstream reaches.

correspondence.component_scope: short lower connecting fragment; Both parts and both fragment joins
correspondence.finding: Both short parts continue within the lower Sarstún lowland corridor. The map and lower image cover the passage and adjoining fragments; there is no separate unsupported transfer here.

correspondence.component_scope: lower wetland sidewater and terminal; All5 parts, initial join, marsh passage and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The final fragment occupies the lower Sarstún river-and-wetland corridor, including the Laguna Grande sidewater vicinity, and reaches the coastal mouth by Cayo Sarstún. The map distinguishes the lagoon and neighboring creeks from the principal river; imagery shows river, wooded wetland, sidewater and coast. The generalized southern bend is retained at corridor scale without a claim of passage through the lagoon center. Small clouds do not leave the overall receiving setting unseen. Distinct supplied source and rendered endpoints are in the same mouth/coastal setting; no offshore extension is invented.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northwestern headward opening and southeastward feeder
correspondence.finding: The upper original depicts the selected opening on a small eastward feeder within the upper valley. It joins the southeastward watercourse continuously depicted and labeled Goodnews River farther along the same valley. The chosen branch and its junction are distinguishable from the adjacent ponds and side drainage.
correspondence.name_scope: Connected upper component of the Goodnews River system; the first small feeder is not given a separately verified scalar name.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Goodnews valley and approach to the lake
correspondence.finding: Repeated Goodnews River labels follow the southward valley and southwest turn toward the lake. The original shows side-stream entries, the Igmiumanik River junction and the connected inlet approach; surrounding mountain divides distinguish this course from nearby independent valleys.
correspondence.name_scope: Named upper Goodnews River; Igmiumanik is an entering tributary, not an alias or separately selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Goodnews Lake, connecting outlet and smaller downstream waterbody
correspondence.finding: The mapped inlet enters the northeastern end of the elongated waterbody labeled Goodnews Lake. Its southwest outlet connects to the smaller downstream lake-like expansion and the westward Goodnews River. The generalized selected lake-margin passage stays within this single connected lake/outlet setting; an exact shoreline or lake-name boundary is not assigned.
correspondence.name_scope: Goodnews Lake is a distinct lake component; the smaller outlet waterbody remains unnamed in this finding.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward lake-outlet reach and southwest middle valley
correspondence.finding: The overview and overlapping middle original continuously depict the Goodnews River below the lakes, past northern tributary entries and through the southwest valley. Repeated direct river labels distinguish its connected channel from neighboring ponds and the separate Middle Fork drainage.

correspondence.component_scope: Canyon Creek and lower-middle Goodnews corridor
correspondence.finding: The mapped trunk continues southwest past Canyon Creek and turns west through the widening, meandering valley. The source shows intervening side-channel joins and the Slate Creek approach. Generalized bends remain in the same continuously depicted Goodnews corridor.
correspondence.name_scope: Goodnews River, with entering tributary names retained only as local junction context.

correspondence.component_scope: Barnum Creek junction and southward lower river
correspondence.finding: The lower original follows the named Goodnews River around the western bend, past the Barnum Creek junction and south into the broad wetland valley. Continuous main-channel and side-channel mapping establishes the selected through-route rather than an inferred crossing between isolated ponds.
correspondence.name_scope: Lower Goodnews River; Barnum Creek is an unselected entering tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle and South Fork junction setting and lower estuary
correspondence.finding: The lower map connects the selected north-side river to the named Middle Fork and South Fork network, then to the broader channel labeled Goodnews River beside the village and bay. Multiple sloughs and islands form a continuously depicted estuarine setting. No unique present-day distributary or allocation of flow is asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: Goodnews receiving river and estuary; Middle Fork and South Fork remain distinct named entering components.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual coastal terminal and final rendered shore extension
correspondence.finding: The selected final westward reach crosses the named lower Goodnews estuary into the Goodnews Bay receiving setting. The final rendered southward extension lies at the adjoining delta shore south of the source endpoint. Both are covered by the same continuous estuary–bay shoreline map; the extension is not a separately named river reach.
correspondence.name_scope: Goodnews River mouth and Goodnews Bay receiving shore; no scalar river name assigned to bay water or shore extension.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and broad eastern arc
correspondence.finding: The upper imagery shows the short chosen opening within a dry sidewash and the connected east-curving mountain drainage. The corridor bends around the intervening upland and opens into the south-trending alluvial valley. The short opening itself receives no invented hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern alluvial collector and southern joining approach
correspondence.finding: Successive joins lie within one visible broad south-trending wash between the western uplands and eastern pale dissected terrain. The selected approach continues into the east–west receiving valley. The state study depicts the northern contributing arm joining the San Ignacio network; imagery supplies the more detailed passage rather than inferring it from a nearby label.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward receiving valley toward the oasis
correspondence.finding: After the northern approach, the selected course turns west through the connected broad wash, including the marked southern bend, and reaches the vegetated San Ignacio settlement corridor. The independent municipal map labels San Ignacio along this receiving drainage.

correspondence.component_scope: Oasis waterbody, crossings and southwest outlet valley
correspondence.finding: The detailed oasis image shows the incoming dry wash, elongated water-filled and densely vegetated bend, nearby settlement and cross-corridor road/embankment features, followed by the same southwest-running floodplain. All parts and their joins remain within this connected oasis-and-valley setting. No separate lake name, dam identity, operating condition or permanently wetted through-thread is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower confined bends and widening wash
